title: Managed embedding split-rollout with per-tenant scoring validation and rollback matrix
creator: Miguel Torres
description:
Goal: provide a standardized, tenant-aware embedding model onboarding flow that supports weighted (split) rollouts, deterministic per-tenant scoring validation against a holdout set, automated rollback triggers, and safe deprecation windows. This ticket covers the orchestration changes, validation heuristics, telemetry requirements, and the rollback matrix necessary to onboard new embedding variants or to deprecate old variants without regressing downstream reranking quality or violating latency SLOs.

Background: Our current embedding onboarding is ad-hoc: some tenants are switched immediately, others get manual canaries. This causes occasional quality regressions (re-ranker AUC drops) and unexpected latency spikes for long-tail tenants. We need a repeatable flow: 1) model-contract checks, 2) internal staging smoke, 3) per-tenant weighted splits, 4) evaluation against tenant-level holdouts, 5) automated rollback when predefined metrics degrade.

Scope and non-goals:
- In scope: control-plane rollout orchestration (weight-splitting by tenant/cohort), model contract validation (dims, dtype, normalization), per-tenant scoring evaluation harness, telemetry dashboards and alerts, safe rollback automation, migration helper for persisted vector stores markers.
- Out of scope: model training, embedding index re-sharding logic in customer DBs, or deep changes to external reranker algorithms (we will rely on existing reranker test harness).

High-level plan:
1) Model contract & smoke tests (ENG): automated checks to verify vector dimensionality, dtype, expected norm distribution, and deterministic-ish outputs for fixed seed prompts. Fail onboarding if contract violated.
2) Canary staging (internal): route internal-test tenants + Redwood-owned traffic to new variant, run regression evals (embedding nearest neighbor consistency + reranker AUC on holdout labels).
3) Tenant-weighted split API: allow per-tenant weight config (0%, 1%, 5%, 25%, 100%) with temporal windows and explicit TTL. Implement consistent hashing to preserve user session stickiness.
4) Per-tenant scoring validation: compute on-ramp metrics per tenant each evaluation window (24h): cosine distribution shift, average nearest-neighbor rank change on canonical queries, reranker AUC/Precision@K on holdout labels. Compare against baseline using configurable gates.
5) Automated rollback matrix: define thresholds for immediate rollback (quality regression > 5% absolute AUC drop OR latency p95 increase > 40% over baseline) and for throttled rollback (sustained drift over N windows). Rollback should be orchestrated with canary-safe steps and a postmortem ticket created automatically.
6) Deprecation policy: implement announcement TTL (90 days for public embeddings) + automatic routing of tenants still pinned at end-of-life to compatibility shim with telemetry.

Acceptance criteria:
- New contract checker runs as part of model registration and blocks model availability if checks fail.
- Tenant-weighted split API exists and can be configured via Console + API; configuration persists and is honored by routing layer.
- Per-tenant evaluation pipeline executes nightly and writes metrics to the embeddings SLI dashboard.
- Rollback automation triggers within 10 minutes of a hard-threshold breach and reverts traffic according to rollback matrix; rollback incidents create a ticket in Linear and notify on #runtime-orchestration.
- No customer-facing quality regressions for controlled rollout (measured by no more than 3% of tenants experiencing >5% AUC drop during staged rollout in pilot).
- Documentation: runbook for SREs and a short Console how-to for PMs and solutions engineers.

Implementation tasks (owner tags):
- ENG: contract-checker service + CI hook (Ravi)
- ENG: tenant-weighted split API + Console UI controls (Aisha Park)
- ENG: evaluation pipeline + holdout harness + metrics (Laura Chen)
- ENG: routing + stickiness changes (Ravi)
- ENG: rollback orchestration + Linear auto-ticketing (SRE lead: Priya Patel)
- PM: rollout guide, deprecation cadence, and customer communication templates (PM: Lina Gomez)
- Docs: Console docs + runbook (Doc ops: Mateo Alvarez)

Telemetry & metrics to collect:
- Per-tenant: avg cosine similarity distribution (baseline vs variant), pctiles (p50/p90/p99) of embedding latencies, nearest-neighbor rank delta on canonical queries, reranker AUC/Precision@10 on holdout, error rates, request size distribution.
- Global: percent of traffic on new variant, count of rollbacks, deploy durations, time-to-detect.

Risk & mitigation:
- Risk: small tenants with sparse query patterns will have noisy metrics leading to false positives. Mitigation: add minimum traffic floor and aggregate small tenants into cohorts.
- Risk: latency regressions on long sequences. Mitigation: add sequence-length stratified metrics and do preflight perf runs on those cohorts.

Rollout pilot plan (4 weeks):
- Week 0: internal smoke test and contract validations on staging models.
- Week 1: 1% tenant split for low-risk cohort (internal + alpha customers). Monitor 24/7.
- Week 2: expand to 5% for medium-risk cohort if metrics stable.
- Week 3: 25% for broad cohort. If stable and no rollbacks, schedule global swap.

Backout & recovery:
- Immediate revert (hard threshold): routing layer flips weights back to baseline; create incident ticket documenting affected tenants and metrics.
- Graceful throttle (soft threshold): pause ramp for N windows and notify PM/SEs for manual review.

Notes about downstream reranker integration:
- Reranker teams must provide an automated eval endpoint or artifact (AUC on canonical holdouts) that our pipeline can hit. If reranker signals are unavailable, treat reranker validation as "not satisfied" for high-risk tenants.

Next steps:
- Align on metric thresholds with PM and Research by 2026-03-07.
- Draft Console UI changes and API contract by 2026-03-12.
- Kick off implementation work in Cycle 2026-W10.

2026-03-04 — Laura Chen: I'll own the nightly evaluation pipeline. Suggest we use a combination of tenant holdouts and synthetic canonical queries for low-traffic tenants. Will propose schema for holdout artifacts by 2026-03-06.
